# cid

> cid is version control for datasets: history, releases, diffs and one-command
> downloads for any files (images, audio, video, text, tables, model weights) and
> the annotations on them. It uses git's verbs with git's meanings. This page is for
> a program or an AI coding agent that has to work with a cid dataset.

If you know git, you know cid: `add` stages, `commit` saves locally (instant,
offline), `push` uploads, `pull` downloads, `checkout` switches version, `status`,
`log` and `diff` read. A release is a tag that never moves. There is no git
repository to manage: cid writes a small readable record into one by itself.

## Ask the tool, not your memory

```
cid help --json
```

prints every command with its usage, its flags, whether it needs the server, what
it changes (`nothing`, `folder` or `server`) and what each exit code means. Prefer
it to anything you remember about cid, this page included.

## Rules that hold for every command

- Add `--json` anywhere on the line. The result is one JSON document on stdout
  (`cid diff`: one JSON line per change, then a summary line). An error is
  `{"error": "...", "exit": N}` on stderr.
- Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 wrong usage; 2 conflict; 3 integrity failure; 4 server or
  network (the same command is safe to run again); 5 access denied.
- Every error message ends with the command to run next. Read it and run that.
- Inside a cloned folder the dataset is implied. Outside one, the address names it.
- Nothing asks a question on stdin, and nothing needs a terminal.

## Getting in without a person

A person uses their SSH key and an address like `cid@host:org/datasets/name`. A
program uses a personal token, made on the dashboard's Tokens page:

```
cid clone https://ci:$CID_PAT@host/org/datasets/name
cd name && CID_TOKEN=$CID_PAT cid pull
```

The token is never written into the folder; pass `CID_TOKEN` to each later command.
Never print a token, and never put one in a commit message or a file.

## Reading a dataset

```
cid clone <address> [--release v1.3.0]     # the latest release unless told
cid clone <address> --split val --class person   # only part of an annotated dataset
cid log --json                              # commits and releases, newest first
cid diff v1.2.0 v1.3.0 --json               # what changed, without downloading either
cid checkout v1.2.0                         # only changed files download
cid status --json                           # offline: branch, edits, unpushed commits
```

Every downloaded file is hash-checked before it appears. Files are shared through a
local cache, so a second clone or a checkout downloads only what is new.

Code that already uses Hugging Face libraries can read a release with no cid
command at all: `HF_ENDPOINT=https://host HF_TOKEN=$CID_PAT`, then
`load_dataset("org/datasets__name", revision="v1.3.0")` (inner slashes of the
dataset's path are written `__`). That door is read-only.

## Changing a file dataset

```
cid add .                       # or one path; hashes and stages
cid commit -m "Add March calls" # local and instant
cid push                        # uploads only what the server lacks
```

- `cid push` refused with exit 2 means someone pushed first: run `cid pull`, then
  `cid push` again.
- `cid pull` lists conflicts (exit 2) when both sides changed the same file. Do not
  choose for the user unless they told you how: each path is decided with
  `cid checkout --mine <path>` or `cid checkout --theirs <path>`, then
  `cid pull --continue`.
- An interrupted `push`, `pull` or `checkout` is finished by running it again.
- `cid tag <name>` makes a release, and `cid branch` and `cid merge` act on the
  server: they are the dataset owner's decisions. Do them only when asked.

## What not to try

- **An annotated dataset's clone is an export.** `cid add` refuses there:
  annotations change in the annotation platform, not in a folder.
- **A folder cloned with `--split` or `--class` is read-only.**
- **A release cannot be moved, renamed or deleted,** and pushed history cannot be
  rewritten. There is no force push, rebase or amend. Fix forward with a new commit
  and a new release.
- **Do not edit anything under `.cid/`.**
- **Do not run git commands to make cid work.** The dataset's git repository is
  written by the server; reading it is fine, pushing to its cid-written files is not.
- **Do not hunt for large files with git tools.** The data is not in git.

## Tables

`cid diff` compares `.csv`, `.parquet` and `.jsonl` files row by row, on the server.
To see which cells changed, the table's key must be declared in a committed
`.cidkeys` file, one rule a line: `people.csv  id`, or `events/  user_id,ts`.
Without one, an edited row shows as one removed and one added.

## Running a server to test against

`deploy/compose/` in the cid repository starts a whole cid on localhost with one
command, with a walkthrough. Its administrator token is given to the CLI as
`CID_SERVER` and `CID_TOKEN`.
